chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'May I be sacrificed for you! I supplicate Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that He grant me the halal (permissible sustenance).' He said: 'Do you know what is the halal?' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! As for that which is with us, it is the goodly earnings.' He said: 'Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: The halal is the food of the Chosen Ones, but say: I ask You from Your extensive sustenance.'

key_terms.قُوتُ الْمُصْطَفَيْنَ: Food/Sustenance of the Chosen Ones (Prophets and Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between asking for halal sustenance and the specific du'a of the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the distinction between the general legal definition of halal (permissible earnings) and the spiritual elevation sought by the Ahl al-Bayt, who emphasize 'extensive sustenance' (rizq al-wasi') as a sign of divine favor. By referencing the practice of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin), the text underscores a Shia scholarly tradition that prioritizes abundance and quality of provision over mere legality, reflecting the high station of the Chosen Ones.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Supplicato to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic that He<sup>azwj</sup> should Grace me the Permissible sustenance’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do you know what is the Permissible (sustenance)?’ So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! As for which is with of the goodly earnings’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘The Permissible livelihood is the food of the ‘Chosen Ones’ (only the Prophets<sup>as</sup> and the Imams<sup>as</sup>), but say, ‘I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> from the extensive sustenance’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn abu Nasr who has said the following: “

Once I asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, please pray for me to Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, so He grants me lawful sustenance.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘Do you know what lawful sustenance is?’ I replied, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, according to our information it is clean earning.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Ali ibn Al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would say, ‘Lawful sustenance is the sustenance of the chosen ones.’ You, however, should say, ‘I pray to You to grant me wide-ranging sustenance.’”
